extra.message: The payroll_bundle_thaw_176 view deserializes user-controlled data via pickle.loads() from request.body and request.GET['blob']. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that executes arbitrary code upon deserialization, leading to full remote code execution on the server.

The payroll_formula_cast_257 view uses eval() on user input from request.GET['expr']. Although builtins are cleared, the expression can still reference variables like 'amount' and 'fee', enabling code execution through crafted expressions that access and modify these values.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command

extra.message: The payroll_jinja_cast_491 view renders user input from request.GET['fragment'] directly into a Jinja2 Template without sanitization. An attacker can craft a template expression that accesses sandbox escape primitives (e.g., __class__, __mro__, __subclasses__) to achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: The payroll_relay_probe_355 view accepts a user-controlled URL via request.GET['endpoint'] and passes it directly to urllib.request.urlopen(). This enables SSRF attacks, allowing access to internal services on the loopback interface or cloud metadata endpoints.

The payroll_xml_fold_521 view parses user-controlled XML body via lxml with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This allows XXE attacks to read local files or perform server-side request forgery through external entity references.

The payroll_mongo_lane_540 view passes user-controlled request body data directly to MongoDB as a query filter without validation. This enables NoSQL injection, allowing an attacker to read or manipulate arbitrary records in the MongoDB database.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in NoSQL Query

extra.message: The payroll_dock_shelf_497 view allows a user-controlled filename from request.GET['name'] to be written directly to the filesystem without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../../') in the filename parameter to write files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: The payroll_done_lane_045 view takes an untrusted redirect URL from request.GET['lane'] and passes it directly to Django's redirect() function. An attacker can use this for open redirect attacks by providing a malicious external URL.

The payroll_trust_drift_550 view uses ssl._create_unverified_context() to create an SSL context that disables certificate verification. This makes the application vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks when connecting to external endpoints.

The payroll_origin_mirror_470 view reflects the request Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and enables credentials. This allows any external site to make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of the victim user.

The payroll_frame_slip_480 view sets X-XSS-Protection to 0 (disabling browser XSS filter) and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string. This weakens multiple security policies and makes the application easier to exploit via client-side attacks.

The payroll_cycle_pulse_043 view catches exceptions and returns the full exception string including type name (debug_type) and message to the user. An attacker can use this to learn internal implementation details such as file system paths, class names, or internal state.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The payroll_vault_stash_236 view accepts and stores sensitive personal data (SSN via request.GET['ssn'] and credit card number via request.GET['card']) without encryption or sanitization. These values are written to a JSON file on disk, creating a high-risk data exposure vulnerability.

The SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is not set. This default secret can be trivially discovered from source code, allowing attackers to forge Django sessions and CSRF tokens.

The default database connection string on line 53 contains hardcoded credentials with default username 'postgres' and password 'postgres'. In production environments without DJANGO_TEST_SQLITE set, this will be used as the fallback database URL.

The seed_demo command uses a hardcoded demo password 'DemoPass123!' for all test accounts and logs it to stdout upon completion (line 107). This exposes credentials in shell history and application logs.
The import_employees view sets the default password 'ChangeMe123!' for all imported users. This hardcoded weak password is used when creating new User accounts from CSV import data.

SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is set to ('HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO', 'https'), but SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE are not explicitly configured. This means sessions may be sent over HTTP connections, allowing session hijacking via man-in-the-middle attacks.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in Session Without Secure Attribute
